title: Transformations of Functions
summary: Starting from toolkit functions, shifts, reflections, and stretches build new graphs. $f(x)+k$ shifts up, $f(x-h)$ shifts right, $-f(x)$ reflects over the x-axis, and $af(x)$ stretches vertically — a fast way to graph without plotting many points.

vertical shift.plain: Moving a graph up or down.

order of transformations.in_class: Horizontal first, then vertical, watching signs.

concept_sections.heading: Toolkit functions
concept_sections.explanation: Memorize the shapes of the parent functions ($x$, $x^2$, $x^3$, $\sqrt{x}$, $|x|$, $1/x$). Transformations reshape these familiar graphs.
math_steps: Identify which parent a formula comes from.

concept_sections.heading: Vertical shifts and stretches
concept_sections.explanation: $f(x)+k$ moves the graph up ($k>0$) or down; $af(x)$ stretches it vertically (|a|>1) or compresses it, and reflects over the x-axis if $a<0$.

concept_sections.heading: Horizontal shifts and stretches
concept_sections.explanation: $f(x-h)$ shifts right by $h$ (note the opposite sign); $f(bx)$ compresses horizontally by $b$, and $f(-x)$ reflects over the y-axis.

concept_sections.heading: Reflections
concept_sections.explanation: A minus outside the function ($-f$) flips it over the x-axis; a minus inside ($f(-x)$) flips it over the y-axis.

concept_sections.heading: Combining transformations
concept_sections.explanation: Apply them in order: horizontal changes (inside the function) first, then vertical (outside). Track the vertex or a key point through each step.
